items.title: Fix benchmark publication and make the website release-aware
items.body:
## Context

The site still published the pre-split benchmark record from the all-in-one `hoplite` process, including the old executable and idle-memory footprint. The benchmark scripts also checked only the response body while the site claimed header equivalence, and measured all Hoplite rounds before all Nginx rounds.

This PR makes the benchmark pipeline authoritative for the new `hoplite-server` data plane and prevents Pages from silently displaying stale measurements.

## Benchmark changes

- validates one stable response contract before measuring any target:
  - HTTP `200`
  - `content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8`
  - `x-hoplite: true`
  - the exact 19-byte response body
  - matching body SHA-256
- alternates target order on every HTTP round and records global sequence/order metadata
- records image identity, executable size, process count, Nginx worker count, idle memory, peak memory and every measured round
- labels Java and Python accurately as standard-library server samples rather than framework benchmarks
- labels the Lua target as Debian `ngx_http_lua`, not a full OpenResty distribution
- adds a single `run-benchmarks.sh` entry point and schema-v2 validator
- requires the HTTP and footprint reports to share commit, Hara revision, Nginx version and response identity

## Publication changes

- replaces the checked-in pre-split numbers with explicit schema-v2 `pending` placeholders
- publishes measured reports as the stable `hoplite-benchmarks` workflow artifact
- builds the website against measured data inside the benchmark workflow
- makes Pages download and re-validate the latest successful artifact before deployment
- falls back to an explicit pending state when no valid artifact exists
- publishes the reports at:
  - `/hoplite/benchmarks/http.json`
  - `/hoplite/benchmarks/footprints.json`

## Website changes

- renders measured and pending states instead of treating missing evidence as zero
- updates the homepage comparison and deployment-envelope panels for `hoplite-server`
- fixes the stale installer and starter-script paths
- distinguishes the stable v0.1.0 all-in-one command from the slim server already merged on `main`
- adds release-aware install, CLI, runtime, production-operation, benchmark and roadmap documentation
- expands Pages verification to reject stale benchmark values, broken scoped links and mismatched raw-report endpoints

- `bash -n` for all benchmark scripts
- pending schema-v2 reports validated with `validate-benchmark-data.sh --allow-pending`
- GitHub workflow YAML parsed successfully
- JSON reports parsed with `jq`
- Astro config and Pages verifier passed `node --check`

items.title: fix(backtest): keep excess_return consistent with corrected benchmark_return
items.body:
## Summary

- BaseEngine.run_backtest() corrects the displayed benchmark_return once an external benchmark's price series contains a non-positive-prior-price bar, but never recomputes excess_return from that same corrected value
- Recomputes excess_return right where benchmark_return is already corrected, so the two fields remain consistent for this corrected benchmark path

## Why

Issue #872 replaced the fragile pct_change-based return calculation with a safe price relative (buy_and_hold_return) for the displayed benchmark_return, after finding it could report numbers like +39,560% where the true return was -42.7%. calc_metrics() has its own internal re-derivation of the same total, still using the exact (1 + bench_ret).prod() - 1 pattern #872 found unsafe. base.py corrects the displayed field but never re-derives excess_return from the corrected value, so the metrics dict can become self-contradictory: benchmark_return reads correctly while excess_return implies a different number, both in the same JSON output the backtest tool returns to the LLM.

I audited every benchmark-derived metric in calc_metrics() (benchmark_return, excess_return, information_ratio, tracking_error, benchmark_beta). Only excess_return is affected. The other three are computed from the per-bar bench_ret series directly, which is already the corrected, #872-safe series by the time it reaches calc_metrics().

## Changes

- agent/backtest/engines/base.py: after the existing benchmark_metadata override, excess_return is recomputed as total_return minus the corrected benchmark_return, but only when an external benchmark was actually resolved. The internal-basket-benchmark path (no config["benchmark"]) is untouched.
- agent/tests/test_benchmark_excess_return_consistency.py: two new regression tests. One runs the real production path (ChinaAEngine.run_backtest, real calc_metrics(), only the network-dependent resolve_benchmark() fetch is stubbed) with a benchmark price series crossing a non-positive-prior-price bar, and asserts total_return minus excess_return equals benchmark_return. The other is a control confirming the fix does not touch excess_return when no external benchmark is configured.

## Test Plan

- [x] Confirmed the load-bearing regression test fails on the pre-fix implementation with a real numeric assertion failure (excess_return read 1.0 instead of 0.5), and passes with the fix
- [x] pytest tests/ -k "engine or backtest or benchmark or metrics" -q --ignore=tests/e2e_backtest (813 passed, 6 skipped, pre-existing)
- [x] black --check on both changed files: pre-existing, unrelated formatting issues in base.py confirmed via diff-isolation against the unpatched file (identical content at shifted line numbers); the new test file is clean
- [x] ruff check on both changed files: all checks passed

## Checklist

- [x] No changes to protected areas (src/agent/, src/session/, src/providers/): this only touches agent/backtest/
- [x] No hardcoded values
- [x] Code follows CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (n/a: internal correctness fix, no public interface change)
- [x] DCO signed-off

items.title: perf+fix: gfortran-vs-ifx benchmark; fix FIX_CYN intent(in) light-sat
items.body:
## Summary

Cross-compiler performance analysis (**gfortran vs ifx**) of the AQUABC pelagic-kinetics OpenMP region, on a 28-core host — plus the small `intent` fix that was needed to build the library with the stricter local ifx.

## Performance (kinetics micro-benchmark, release+OpenMP)

**Single-thread (µs/step) — code generation:**

| nkn | gfortran | ifx | ifx faster |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 100 | 555 | 417 | 1.33× |
| 500 | 3633 | 2021 | 1.80× |
| 1000 | 9639 | 4923 | **1.96×** |

**ifx generates ~2× faster serial code** (better auto-vectorization).

**Strong scaling, nkn=1000 (vs own 1-thread):**

| threads | gfortran | ifx |
|---|---:|---:|
| 8 | **7.03×** | 3.71× |
| 16 | 6.65× | **3.83×** |

gfortran scales further off its slower baseline; the two **converge in absolute time** (~1350 µs/step @8t). Best absolute: **ifx 1284 µs/step @16t** vs gfortran 1371 @8t (~6% edge, at ~2× the build time: ~60 s vs ~32 s). Full write-up in `docs/OPENMP_PERFORMANCE.md`.

## Fixes enabling the ifx build

- **`benchmark_openmp.sh`** — compiler-appropriate driver flags (ifx: `-qopenmp -O3 -xHost`; gfortran: `-fopenmp -O3 -march=native`) + `THREADS` override.
- **`FIX_CYANOBACTERIA`** — `FIX_CYN_LIGHT_SAT` was `intent(in)` but `LIM_LIGHT` *writes* it (it's an output). The stricter local **ifx 2026.1.0 rejects this (error #6780)** where gfortran and CI's ifx tolerate it. Changed to `intent(inout)`, matching the DIA/CYN/OPA light-sat declarations. **Behaviour-preserving** — gfortran 0D golden unchanged (526×22).

items.title: Phase 1: codec-series builder validation, nd-delta round-trip, and live benchmark harness with baselines
items.body:
Implements [roadmap Phase 1](docs/development/roadmap/phase-1-baselines-and-series.md) — the phase that gates all later codec work. It delivers a usable product on day one without implementing any new codec: the **nd-delta** family (composed entirely of existing Zarr codecs), a fully validated tri-language `codec_series` builder, and a live benchmark harness with committed baselines. All four Phase 1 acceptance criteria are met and ticked in the roadmap doc.

## What changed

### 1. Cross-language `codec_series` equality, enforced in CI
- **`fixtures/codec-series/matrix.json`** — 148 shared cases (8 axis layouts × chunk-shape variants × dtypes × 3 families, plus option-override and error cases) with committed expected pipeline JSON, generated by `scripts/gen-series-fixtures.py`.
- Per-language matrix tests: Rust (`crates/ndic-zarr/tests/series_matrix.rs`), Python (`tests/test_codec_series_matrix.py`), TypeScript (`test/codec-series.test.ts`).
- **`scripts/ci/check-series-equality.py`** rewritten to drive all three implementations across every case — the Rust side through the real `ndic series` CLI, exercising option mapping — asserting byte-identical JSON and error agreement. `ci.yml` gains a `typescript` job and runs pytest in the `python` job.

### 2. nd-delta end-to-end round-trip via `zarr-python`
- `tests/test_nd_delta_roundtrip.py`: builder-authored pipelines round-trip bit-exactly through zarr-python v3 — tczyx with zstd/lz4 backends, zyx, transpose-free yx, partial edge chunks, and uint16 wrap-around extremes — on a deterministic synthetic microscopy volume (`bench/py/synthetic.py`: seeded drifting Gaussian blobs + Poisson shot noise).

### 3. Full `ndic series` CLI option set
- `--decorrelate` / `--add-decorrelate` / `--remove-decorrelate`, `--lift`, `--xy-levels`, `--lossy`, `--delta-backend`, `--zfp-rate`, with unit tests across all three families and error paths.

### 4. Live benchmark harness with committed baselines
- **`ndic-bench-core`**: `BenchOutput` (samples + `bytes_in`/`bytes_out`), `BenchRecord` save/load, `Baseline` manifest IO, and a diff comparer with two gates — median ≥ 10 % **and** beyond the baseline's σ envelope (time), and ≥ 2 % compressed-size growth (ratio, deterministic across machines).
- **`ndic-bench`** `run`/`compare`/`list` are now real: records under `target/benchmarks/<git-hash>/<config>/`, `--format ascii|markdown|json|csv`, `--gate time|ratio|both`, exit codes 0/1/2 (all verified, including tripped-gate paths).
- **`bench/py/run_nd_delta.py`**: the Phase 1 lanes — `nd-delta-zstd`, `nd-delta-lz4` vs the plain `blosc-zstd` reference — measured through zarr-python, emitting the same record schema so `ndic-bench compare` gates them like Rust workloads.
- First baselines committed under `bench/baselines/main/` (30 samples; provenance in `manifest.json`). `bench-pr-gate.yml` runs the lanes on PRs and gates on **ratio only**, since CI runners differ from the baseline capture machine and the σ envelope is machine-class-specific.

## Notable finding

On the committed synthetic fixture, nd-delta-zstd compresses slightly *worse* than plain blosc-zstd (0.562 vs 0.543): uint16 delta wrap-around flips high bits (hurting bitshuffle) and Poisson shot noise dominates z-correlation. Verified across smoother/lower-noise fixture variants rather than tuning the fixture to flatter the family — the baselines record the honest result. Phase 2's `nd_lift` (proper sign handling) is the expected fix; nd-delta-lz4 is the fastest encoder of the three lanes.

## Verification

- `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` (0 warnings), `cargo test --workspace`, wasm32 check, `cargo doc` — all clean
- `scripts/ci/check-series-equality.py`: 148/148 cases identical across Rust/Python/TypeScript
- 156 pytest + 149 vitest tests passing

**Revised per review feedback** (thank you — this caught real issues):

1. **`provenance_validated_solved_rate` (0.88%) is no longer called a "floor" or "lower bound."** Precisely, it's the fraction of targets with a complete stock route where every step passes the atom-balance check AND is positively confirmed by its own originating rule's current validator. It is **not** a measured chemical-accuracy rate, and **not** a proven lower bound on true correctness — that would require the validator to have zero false positives, which hasn't been shown (1 of the 44 `validated` routes itself fails atom-balance; a diagnostic sample has 14/864 `Valid`-but-imbalanced steps). The internal JSON field name is unchanged for compatibility; every public-facing occurrence now uses "current-validator-confirmed rate" as the plain-language label plus the caveat above.
2. **Softened the false-negative framing.** Previously said "a large share of Invalid verdicts may be false negatives." Now: an *unknown* fraction of the 72.2% `Invalid`-but-atom-balanced steps in a diagnostic n=300 sample may be validator false negatives, and the remainder may be genuine rule/route errors — the split is unmeasured, not estimated.
3. **Removed the numeric README badge** (`USPTO-50k raw 20.1% (corrected)`) — a bare raw-rate badge risked being read as a quality-inclusive success rate, contradicting the page's own framing. Replaced with a non-numeric `USPTO-50k corrected baseline` badge; all three nested numbers now live only in the body table.
4. **Building-block count corrected to the actually-loaded value.** `ChemEnv::bb_count()` after `ChemEnv::load("data/building_blocks.smi")` = **402** (not 475, which was a naive `grep -cv '^#'` line count from an earlier draft; not the older "509" figure either). Breakdown: 449 trimmed non-comment lines → 3 fail to parse → 446 parse → 44 duplicate after canonicalization → 402 unique. This is a documentation-accuracy fix only — the actual benchmark run always used the real 402-compound loaded set via the same `ChemEnv::load()` path, so the measured solved/atom-balanced/validated counts are unaffected. Applied consistently across both READMEs, both benchmark docs, and the provenance doc. Historical "509"/"480"/"463" figures elsewhere are kept in their historical rows but now explicitly marked as legacy documentation values, not re-verified against `bb_count()`. Bonus: found and fixed two more stale, unverified counts while in there — the embedded `DEFAULT_BUILDING_BLOCKS` fallback documented as "509-BB / 20-rule" is actually 152 unique / 28 rules (verified), and a source comment claiming "~300 entries" for the same constant was wrong too.
5. **Neutralized the competitor-comparison language.** Removed "fairest like-for-like comparison" and "uncorroborated found-a-route rates." Now: `raw_solved_rate` is described as "the closest available RENKIN metric to the published route-finding success rates of the other planners," with an explicit statement that stock size/template library/target set/search budget/route-quality checks differ and the table doesn't establish RENKIN as better or worse.
6. **Public-label tables added.** Every metric table now shows a "Public label" column (Search-to-stock rate / Atom-balance-filtered rate / Current-validator-confirmed rate) alongside the internal metric name, with an explicit note underneath that the three are a nested series over one denominator and none is an experimentally-verified synthesis success rate or human-chemist-reviewed route-accuracy figure.
7. **Phase 31 framing**: "Phase 31 corrected-baseline publication is complete; validator fidelity analysis (separating real rule errors from validator false negatives) remains an explicit, open follow-up" — not "Phase 31 complete."

**No re-measurement was performed for this revision** — same binary, same rule set, same validator, same `data/bench_chunks_phase31_final_e20dc8c` raw output. Only documentation wording and the building-block count (a config-description fix, not a result change) were corrected.

## Why the raw rate dropped again (24.01% provisional → 20.09% here)

Expected and by design — 31.11 removed three rules that were fabricating "solved" routes by silently discarding a halogen atom (e.g. chlorobenzene → benzene, Cl unaccounted for). `atom_balanced_solved_rate` rising in the same direction (14.00% → 15.41% over all 4,907, recomputed for comparability) corroborates that this is fake-positive removal, not a capability regression — same pattern as the earlier `aryl_carboxylation_retro` fix.

**What's explicitly still invalidated and NOT re-measured**, marked inline everywhere it appears (not just a top-of-page notice): cascade search (95.9%) and ChEMBL OOD (81.8%). Only USPTO-50k Stage 1 single-pass was re-run this session.

## Changes

- `README.md` / `README_ja.md`: non-numeric corrected-baseline badge, public-label metric table in the Benchmark section, historical 78.0%/95.9%/81.8% figures relabeled pre-fix/invalidated everywhere they appear, building-block counts corrected to 402 (measured) throughout with historical rows marked as unverified legacy values, competitive-landscape wording neutralized.
- `docs/benchmark.md` / `docs/benchmark_ja.md`: same, plus explicit inline warnings on the OOD and Failure Taxonomy sections (both un-re-measured).
- `scripts/aggregate_bench_results.py`: added `atom_balanced_solved_rate` (previously only `pct_atom_balanced_of_solved` existed, a *different* denominator — solved-count, not total-target-count — not directly comparable to `raw_solved_rate`; catching this before publishing avoided a second, subtler version of the exact inconsistency Phase 31 exists to eliminate).
- `src/lib.rs`: one-line comment fix (`DEFAULT_BUILDING_BLOCKS` "~300 entries" → verified 160 raw / 152 unique). No behavior change.

## Known follow-up (not this PR)

- Validator fidelity analysis (72.2% Invalid-but-balanced, real-error-vs-false-negative split) — open, tracked in `tasks/todo.md` 31.12's second half.
- `renkin-bench compare`'s dedup key doesn't work on USPTO-50k-shaped input (found during the benchmark-integrity audit, PR #32) — matters for any future before/after diff.
- Cascade (Stage 2) and ChEMBL OOD re-measurement against the corrected rule set — not started.

## Gate note

`cargo fmt --check` and `cargo clippy -- -D warnings` (CI's actual Lint command) are clean. `cargo clippy --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` currently fails on unmodified `master` itself (confirmed via `git diff origin/master -- src/chem_env.rs src/python.rs` = empty — this PR touches neither file) — pre-existing dead-code/lint findings in `src/chem_env.rs` test helpers and pyo3-gated closures in `src/python.rs`, unrelated to and predating this PR. items.body:
## What

Replaces every `[TBP]` placeholder across the SOTA/performance tables with **independently verified numbers** — not copied from the results summary at face value, but recomputed from the raw per-sample telemetry and cross-checked against every chart. Also closes the last of B3 (two docs still carried the old fabricated-title-style citations already fixed in `README.md`).

`scripts/results/` (JSON telemetry, PNGs, the corrected summary) is un-gitignored and committed — the docs now embed images and link data files from it, so it needs to actually exist in the repo for anyone else.

## Verification methodology

Every headline number was **independently recomputed from the raw 1000-sample / 88-probe arrays** in `benchmark_results.json` (not trusted from the summary doc) and cross-checked pixel-for-pixel against the PNGs. All matched exactly: intent accuracy (85.7%), full 4×4 confusion matrix, ToM MAE (0.032/0.041), Recall@K (81.8/87.5/87.5/93.2%), resource footprint (1,266 MB / 0.99 W), paralinguistic precision (95.3%/94.4%).

## Two fabrication bugs found and fixed (not just documented)

In `scripts/research/cognitive_metrics_eval.py`:
1. **`module3_memory_actr()`** silently fell back to `np.random.seed(42)`-generated **synthetic** latency-scaling numbers whenever real progression data was missing — that fabricated curve (flat 15ms vs. rising to 50ms) is what `cognitive_rag_recall.png`'s right panel actually plots. The real underlying data tells a much smaller story (~170ms→174ms vs. ~170ms→181ms, ~4% apart). **Fixed to raise instead of fabricate.**
2. **`module4_conflict_resolver()`**'s barge-in "stop latency" (104.3ms mean, 7.72ms std) was fake Gaussian noise (`np.random.normal`) sprinkled onto a real composed constant, and the "baseline" 479.9ms was a fully invented, uncited number. **Fixed to report the composed constant directly, with its provenance, and no fabricated baseline.**

items.title: Sprint 105: detach the repo from the machine that grew it
items.body:
Template readiness: make the repo carry as little of one machine as possible. 575 → **577 tests**, clippy 0, fmt clean. *ADR-096.*

> **Note on commit count:** rebased onto sprint 104, so until [#63](https://github.com/crussella0129/Animus_Ferric/pull/63) merges this shows both commits. The base is `main`, so it resolves itself the moment #63 lands. (Rebased rather than branched independently because both sprints append to `decisions.md`/`README.md` and a `git merge-tree` check showed they conflict.)

## The repo had already learned this lesson once — and applied it to exactly one file

Sprint 97 (ADR-088) found a **tracked** `docker/.env` pinning `MODELS_PATH` to one machine's NAS drive. Because it was tracked it overrode the compose default on *every* checkout, and `docker compose up` failed anywhere that drive wasn't mapped. The fix was the ordinary pattern — untrack, ship `.env.example`, gitignore the original.

This applies that pattern everywhere else it holds.

## Untracked what the tooling itself calls ephemeral

**`sprints/` had 139 tracked files while already listed in `.gitignore`.** A gitignore rule does not untrack what is already tracked, so the rule added around sprint 33 silently did nothing for the files that existed when it landed — and the template shipped 139 files its own ignore block describes as *"regenerable; the real outcome lives in the per-task git commits + decisions.md"*.

Also `scratch/` and `benchmarks/results.jsonl`. **`git rm --cached` only — every file stays on disk.**

## One of these was behavioural, not cosmetic

`benchmarks/model_profiles.json` is read back at runtime by ADR-029, where a stored `measured_level` overrides the parameter-count prior **in both directions**. The tracked file carried `qwen2.5-coder-7b → 6/Large`, measured here.

ADR-029 established that a profile **miss** is a safe no-op. Nobody had asked what a profile **hit from someone else's machine** means. Measured, same command and model name in two trees:

| tree | `model_profiles.json` | tier selected |
|---|---|---|
| fresh clone | absent | **Nano** (params prior) |
| this machine | present, `measured_level: 6` | **Large** |

For a project whose thesis is *measure, don't assume*, shipping unearned measurements as defaults is backwards. Now gitignored, with a `model_profiles.example.json` whose measurements are `null` — the shape without the claim.

## Machine identity out of the Rust fixtures

The sharpest leaks weren't paths, they were **identity**: a real tailnet IP, MagicDNS suffix, hostname and node id in `server.rs`; device names, tailnet IPs and the owner's **account handle** in `retriever.rs`.

Their comments said "captured from this machine", which is why they were faithful — and faithful is what the tests need. But **the shape is what the tests assert; the identity was incidental.** Every fixture keeps its exact structure with documentation values, addresses staying inside Tailscale's real `100.64.0.0/10` CGNAT range so they remain representative. **All assertions still pass, which is itself the evidence that none were asserting identity.**

## Defaults nobody else could satisfy

`run_benchmarks.ps1` had a hardcoded `D:\Models\gguf\…` GGUF default — now a required parameter, because no default beats one that works on a single machine. `.env.example` teaches the shape instead of one drive letter. `docker-compose.yml`'s `../../Animus/Models` is a *suite-layout* assumption rather than a machine path, so it stays, commented as such.

## A one-time cleanup decays, so it's a test now

`template_hygiene.rs` fails on shapes that **can only be identity** — a `tail<digits>.ts.net` MagicDNS suffix, a concrete home directory, a `192.168.x.y` LAN address — while deliberately not matching *topics* (this repo's prose is full of the word "tailscale"; none of that is a leak).

**The guard's own self-test found a hole in the guard.** The first version matched `\Users\name` in single-backslash form only — but the likeliest place for a leaked path is *inside a Rust string literal*, where `C:\Users\alice` is written `"C:\\Users\\alice"` and reaches the matcher doubled. It would have missed exactly the case it exists for.

The repo scan is also shown **failing against a planted leak**, naming both matched rules — because a guard that has never rejected anything is not known to reject anything (sprint 96's skip-and-pass, sprint 101's false positive).

## Fresh-clone verification

`git rm --cached` leaves files on disk, so a local build proves nothing about what a template user receives. Cloned the branch to a temp directory: `sprints/` absent, `scratch/` absent, `benchmarks/` holds only the example; **`cargo test --workspace` → 577 passed**; and `ferric query --mock` completes with **no `model_profiles.json`**, so ADR-029's "a miss is a safe no-op" is exercised rather than cited — which matters, because this PR makes it the default state for every new user.

## Incidental find, from the merge this sprint caused

`agent-tasks/completed-tasks.md` contained **215 NUL bytes** — a UTF-16LE fragment appended into a UTF-8 file, the signature of a PowerShell `>>` redirect. Git therefore classified the project's completed-task log as **binary**: no line diffs, no auto-merge. That is why a conflict where both sides merely appended to the end could not resolve itself. Re-encoded to UTF-8, content byte-identical after decoding.

## Deliberately not done

**`decisions.md`, `agent-tasks/` and git history are not scrubbed.** The ADRs are the reasoning record; rewriting them to remove the machine that produced the measurements would falsify the evidence they cite.

That choice has a consequence, stated in the open rather than buried: **`decisions.md` still contains tailnet addresses and device names, and untracking never removes anything from history.** If this template is published, that history goes with it. Removing it needs a history rewrite — a destructive force-push on a shared branch — which is the owner's call and was not taken unasked.

## Summary

- replace the Winnow combinator parser with a handwritten, byte-offset parser
- preserve parsed values, error messages, and caret positions for the existing grammar
- remove the direct `winnow` dependency
- add snapshot coverage for successful extensions and parser/error boundaries
- add a Divan benchmark suite for parser success and failure paths

## Compatibility

All pre-existing snapshot files remain byte-for-byte unchanged.

I also compared the old and new parsers over 34,228 generated expressions covering all five fields, default and hashed modes, literals, lists, ranges, steps, `L`, `W`, `#`, malformed input, overflow, Unicode, and top-level field boundaries. Outside inputs affected by the two intentional syntax fixes below, every parsed `Ok` value and complete `Err` string matched exactly.

## Intentional behavior fixes

1. Month and weekday names are now ASCII case-insensitive. The crate documentation already specifies this and gives mixed-case examples, but the old parser only accepted uppercase names.
2. Numeric literals now accept leading zeros, including range bounds, steps, and nth-weekday values. This is conventional cron syntax, and the existing documentation already used `00` in a step expansion example; the contract is now stated explicitly.

A success snapshot covers both fixes with `00 04 01 Jan-Mar/02 Mon-Fri UTC`.

There is one direct diagnostic consequence for invalid expressions in these newly recognized forms: the parser now consumes the valid case-insensitive name or full leading-zero number before reporting the remaining error. For example, `JanX` points at `X`, while `060` reports that 60 is out of range instead of reporting a malformed second digit. Both diagnostics have dedicated snapshots. Their `Err` classification is unchanged, but the text and caret are intentionally more precise.

## Performance

Measured with Divan 0.1.21 in the release benchmark profile on an Apple M4 Max using Rust 1.95.0. Each revision was run twice in alternating old/new order with `--min-time 1 --sample-count 100`; the table averages the two reported medians. Lower latency is better.

| Benchmark | Winnow | Handwritten | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fields / scalar | 1.666 µs | 472.3 ns | 3.53× |
| Fields / wildcard | 3.457 µs | 2.520 µs | 1.37× |
| Fields / complex | 3.999 µs | 1.749 µs | 2.29× |
| With timezone / scalar | 1.724 µs | 490.6 ns | 3.51× |
| With timezone / wildcard | 3.499 µs | 2.541 µs | 1.38× |
| With timezone / complex | 4.291 µs | 1.833 µs | 2.34× |
| Hashed | 1.822 µs | 425.5 ns | 4.28× |

| Failure / late out of range | 4.499 µs | 1.999 µs | 2.25× |
| Failure / unknown timezone | 4.832 µs | 2.291 µs | 2.11× |

The handwritten parser is faster in every measured case. Wildcard-heavy inputs improve less because constructing and dropping the expanded result sets dominates their runtime; simple, hashed, and complex parsing paths show the largest parser-specific gains.

items.title: fix(instance): wait for a real public IPv4 and make creates recoverable
items.body:
Closes #2. **Stacked on #4** — review that one first; the base will retarget to `main` when #4 merges.

## Problem

Reconcile returned the attributes of the single GET issued after create, and Vultr reports `main_ip: "0.0.0.0"` while an instance is still provisioning. That placeholder was persisted as converged state and published by every consumer of `mainIp`, DNS records included. Because Alchemy reuses the attributes of no-op resources, later deployments never repaired it.

## Change

**Readiness.** Poll `GET /instances/{id}` until `main_ip` is a routable public IPv4, bounded by `readinessTimeout` (default 15 min) with a capped backoff (`readinessPollInterval`, default 5s) and structured per-attempt logs. Exhaustion fails with a typed `VultrNotReady` carrying id, attempts, and the last observed `main_ip`/`status`/`server_status`. `disablePublicIpv4: true` skips the wait. Placeholder, private, loopback, link-local, CGNAT, documentation, benchmark, multicast, reserved, IPv6, and malformed values are never returned as a public `mainIp`.

**Recoverable creates — the prerequisite.** A long poll widens the window between an accepted `POST /instances` and Alchemy persisting attributes, so this lands with it rather than after it:

- Every instance carries an `alchemy-vultr-recover-<hash>` tag beside the user's tags, keyed on stack + stage + resource FQN + create-only props. Deliberately **not** on the Alchemy `instanceId`: a restarted replacement mints a fresh generation, and recovery keyed to the old one would miss the VM Vultr already accepted (per the analysis in the issue thread).
- Reconcile looks for that tag before creating, and fails closed with `VultrAmbiguousRecovery` when more than one VM claims it.
- New `VultrClient.postOnce` (no transient retry) plus a create loop that re-checks for the ownership tag after every ambiguous failure. `client.post` retries 5xx/transport internally, which for a create can provision several VMs from one reconcile; now a lost create response costs exactly one `POST /instances`.

## Tests

`test/instance-readiness.test.ts` — 41 cases: the full IPv4 classification table, placeholder → assigned transition, single-GET fast path, VPC-only skip, typed timeout contents, 404 not treated as provisioning state, lost create response asserting exactly one POST, recovery from a later generation id, tag stability across generations/props/FQN/stage, ambiguous fail-closed, no adoption of an untagged instance the server-side filter returned anyway, user tags preserved, and update/delete staying on the same physical id.

## Migration

The fix prevents future bad creates but does not refresh an existing stable resource. Stacks already holding `mainIp: "0.0.0.0"` need one targeted reconcile (e.g. a durable label/tag change) or a state sync to repair the recorded address and the DNS records derived from it. Called out in the changeset.

Adds `evals/golden_dataset.json`, the committed benchmark input that `.cursor/rules/testing-evals.mdc` and the `@RunEvals` skill both already assume exists. Until now the evaluation suite had no dataset to score against, which is why the CI quality gate on schema validity and grounding was unenforced.

The dataset pins six scenarios across three policy documents. Each one fixes the webhook input, the chunks retrieval is expected to return, and the recommendation the agent is expected to produce, so Recall@k, grounding, and schema validity can all be scored deterministically against a stable target.

| Scenario | Category | Expected decision | Policy |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| TEST-01 | Baseline entitlement happy path | APPROVE | POL-2026-01-DGW |
| TEST-02 | SoD conflict, edit plus billing export | DENY | POL-2026-01-DGW |
| TEST-03 | Elevated privilege and time-boxing | ESCALATE | POL-2026-02-SEC |
| TEST-04 | SoD conflict, code approver plus deployer | DENY | POL-2026-02-SEC |
| TEST-05 | Baseline commercial opportunity edit | APPROVE | POL-2026-03-CRM |
| TEST-06 | Non-commercial bulk export, DPO review | ESCALATE | POL-2026-03-CRM |

Coverage is deliberately balanced across the decision space: two APPROVE, two DENY, and two ESCALATE, with both denials driven by Separation of Duties conflicts rather than missing entitlements. TEST-06 is the only multi-chunk case, requiring retrieval to surface two distinct sections and the agent to cite both.

A second commit refreshes `docs/CODEBASE_REFERENCE.md`, which had drifted. It now points at commit `baacee6` instead of `0e11a1c` and distinguishes the two live request paths: the HITL sync path wired end to end through retrieval, decision engine, persistence, and audit, versus the webhook async path that still terminates at `MockDownstreamService` without touching the AI subsystem.

- Prettier: clean, no files reformatted

It holds 6 scenarios with decisions APPROVE, DENY, ESCALATE, DENY, APPROVE, ESCALATE and expected-chunk counts of 1, 1, 1, 1, 1, and 2 matching the citation counts per scenario. Every scenario carries the six required snake_case keys, and no string value contains a stray embedded newline.

No schema, API, or database impact. This adds a static test fixture and a documentation update; no application code changes.

The `decision` values use the `APPROVE | DENY | ESCALATE` enum from `RecommendationSchema` in `apps/backend/src/modules/ai/schemas/recommendation.schema.ts`, so the dataset's expected outputs stay aligned with the production Zod contract rather than drifting into a parallel vocabulary. The review also found `ca-x-nord` — a **fifth** descendant of `ca-x-medieval` that revision 1's blast-radius claim missed.

## What this PR does now

Two rules, `CA_DEGEM_S` and `CA_DEGEM_SH`, using the existing `sandhi_rules` machinery. **No engine change.** Where a word ends in the same sibilant the next begins with, the coda one is deleted (Wheeler 2005, *The Phonology of Catalan*, §10.4; Recasens 1993 §5): `més són` → `ˈme ˈson`, `dos savis` → `ˈdo ˈsaβis`, `és seca` → `ˈe ˈsɛkə`. The `4catac` Central subset writes all twenty of its `/s#s/` boundaries with a single `[s]`.

### Blast radius: all five descendants of `ca-x-medieval`, stated

| spec | gets the rules | why |
|---|---|---|
| `ca` | yes | 4catac Central: 20/20 boundaries single `[s]` |
| `ca-x-occidental` | yes | 4catac North-Western, measured improvement |
| `ca-x-valencia` | yes | 4catac Valencian, measured improvement |
| `ca-x-nord` | yes | **no gold set** — Wheeler's statement extended by descent, stated as a prediction in the rule notes, not a measured result |
| `ca-x-balear` | **no** | 44/44 boundaries are `[t t͡s]`, assimilation not deletion |
| `ca-x-medieval` | **no** | ancestor stays clean so Balearic cannot inherit it |

`ca-x-balear.json`'s `notes` records the exclusion and the evidence, so the next person does not "fix" the asymmetry.

### Scope is narrow on three axes, all measured

1. **Identical sibilants only.** Before a sibilant differing in place or voicing the coda sibilant *voices* — `petits juguen` → `pəˈtidz ˈʒuɣən` (Wheeler 2005 §5.3), already handled by `CA_FINAL_TS_VOICING`. A broader version scored better on 4catac but contradicted cited `spain_romance_tts` gold rows; rejected.
2. **Sibilants only.** A cross-word stop or nasal geminate stays long (`tot tancat`, `constantment` `[kunstamˈmen]`). Extending deletion to `t d p b k ɡ m n ɲ l ʎ ɾ r` was measured and worsened *every* Catalan 4catac row.
3. **Voiceless sibilants only.** Revision 1's `CA_DEGEM_Z` and `CA_DEGEM_ZH` were **unfirable and are dropped**: word-final devoicing means no word surfaces with final `[z]`/`[ʒ]` when the sandhi engine matches contexts, and the engine matches against the ORIGINAL words, never against an earlier rule's output. Consequence, now pinned rather than hidden: `dos zeros` → `ˈdoz ˈzɛɾus`, a cross-word geminate. Collapsing it needs ordering the engine does not offer. Documented in the rule notes and in `test_voiced_sibilant_boundary_is_a_known_gap`.

## Per-dialect numbers

`4catac`, expert-annotated (Projecte AINA/BSC, IEC guidelines, multi-annotator consensus), full set, N=160 per accent. Lower is better.

| spec | before (`dev`) | after | delta | espeak |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `ca` | 0.0986 | **0.0962** | −0.0024 | 0.0403 |
| `ca-x-occidental` | 0.1026 | **0.1000** | −0.0026 | 0.0546 |
| `ca-x-valencia` | 0.0851 | **0.0826** | −0.0025 | 0.0476 |
| `ca-x-balear` | 0.1997 | 0.1997 | 0.0000 | 0.0798 |
| `ca-x-nord` | — | — | no gold set | — |

Balearic returning to its `dev` value is the intended outcome, not a miss. `ca-x-medieval` has `spain_romance_tts` gold (exact-match, 20 rows) and is unaffected.

**espeak still leads on all four accents — this narrows the gap, it does not close it.**

## Stale CI baseline closed

`benchmarks/results_ci_sample.json`'s four `4catac` rows were still at pre-#802 values (`ca` 0.1069, `ca-x-balear` 0.2033, `ca-x-occidental` 0.1150, `ca-x-valencia` 0.0944) — the regression gate was comparing against a baseline two PRs old. All four are regenerated here at the CI sample limit via the same `build_scoreboard` row construction `--ci-sample` uses, including `ca-x-balear` (0.2033 → 0.1997) which this PR does not otherwise touch.

## Tests

`tests/test_catalan_phonology.py`:

- `test_cross_word_sibilant_degemination` — 4 phrases × 4 dialects
- `test_balearic_does_not_degeminate` — **the refuting case as a regression test**: asserts `ca-x-balear` and `ca-x-medieval` do NOT degeminate `és sa` / `més són`. Confirmed to FAIL against revision 1's ancestor placement.
- `test_unlike_sibilants_voice_rather_than_delete`
- `test_sibilant_degemination_is_sibilant_only`
- `test_sibilant_degemination_does_not_preempt_voicing`
- `test_voiced_sibilant_boundary_is_a_known_gap` — `dos zeros`
- `test_cross_word_vowel_elision_is_a_known_gap`

16 of these were observed FAILING against `origin/dev` before the spec change and passing after.

## What remains

- **Cross-word vowel elision — the largest single driver, out of scope.** `va anar` is `[baˈna]` in the gold; the engine gives `ˈba əˈna`. `que es` is `[kəs]`. Wheeler 2005 §10.1 vowel contact. The `sandhi_rules` regexes see the two words as separate strings and can only rewrite within one, so deleting a vowel conditioned on the next word's first segment needs new engine surface. 162 spurious `[ə]` insertions on `ca` alone. Pinned in `test_cross_word_vowel_elision_is_a_known_gap`, asserting the wrong-but-current output.
- **Balearic `/s#s/` → `[t t͡s]`** — real, cited, unmodelled. `ca-x-balear`'s 0.1997 will not move until someone builds it. Separate piece of work.
- **`/s # z/` cross-word geminate** — needs sandhi rules to see post-voicing forms; engine-level.
- **Rhotic `r↔ɾ`** — not linking. `ca-x-balear`'s gold writes coda `[ɾ]` where the spec emits `[r]` (102 occurrences, that accent's largest confusion pair) while `ca`'s gold writes `[r]` in the same position: a per-annotator notation split inside `4catac`, word-internal. Not forced.
- **`benchmarks/comparison.json` `ca` rows** are stale by the deltas above; `o2i_lex_per` and `espeak_rules_per` need an espeak rules-only build unavailable here, and a partial row would mix harness epochs.
- ~~`scripts/error_analysis.py` misleads on sentence datasets~~ — **already fixed on `dev` by #816**, which this branch is rebased onto. That bug is what produced this campaign's original (wrong) `z↔s` diagnosis.

items.title: fix(interp): let a committing flush pass through a live ref operand
items.body:
## Summary

`BenchmarkCall_IndirectRecursiveFib/default` drops from **598,302 → 80,548 ns/op** (7.4x). It previously ran *slower* than `threaded`; it now beats it by 6.9x.

The cause was not per-call overhead — **nothing compiled at all**. The profiler recorded exactly one attempt, `outcome=rejected, reason=lowering-rejected`, and zero native entries.

`arm64Lowerer.flush` refused to commit whenever any live operand was a `KindRef`:

```go
if v.kind == types.KindRef && commit {
    return false
}
```

`selfCall` is the only caller that reaches that loop with live values (`tailLoop` pops all args and bails unless the operand stack is empty). `indirectRecursiveFib` passes its own callee as a ref *argument*, so a `KindRef` was always live there and the whole compile was rejected. `observe()` never retries a rejected anchor, so the function stayed interpreted for the process lifetime. `recursiveFib`'s args are i32-only, which is the entire difference between 38 us and 598 us.

## Why this is refcount-safe

The real hazard is only the **raw** marker: `box()` materializes and retains it *because the interpreter frame being rebuilt will release it* — and a commit rebuilds no frame, so nothing balances that retain. A **non-raw** ref already carries the retain taken when it was pushed (`localGet` retains before `ctx.push`), and `box()` returns it with no extra retain. Committing therefore *transfers* that single ownership edge to the stack — precisely what the ordinary inlined call path already does when it stores arguments and truncates `ctx.values` without releasing.

So the check is simply over-broad. Rejecting only raw refs is both necessary and sufficient: raw markers are produced only fused with their immediate consumer and cannot survive as an unrelated live operand at a self-call.

## Test plan

- [x] New `TestARM64_SelfCallWithRefArg` — differential-tests the JIT result against a `WithThreshold(-1)` threaded reference, and asserts a trace is actually installed (`entryFunction`, `vm_jit_native_entries_total > 0`).
- [x] **Verified the test guards the fix**: reverting the one-line change makes `compiles natively` fail (`compiled.module` nil). The correctness subtest alone passes either way via interpreted fallback, which is why the install assertion carries the regression.
- [x] `go test -race ./...` green (both modules); `make fuzz` clean; `gofmt`/`go vet` clean.
- [x] Benchmarks re-measured on this branch at canonical `benchtime=1s -count=5`; `docs/benchmarks.md` updated with those medians.

Eager `jit` (threshold 0) is unchanged at ~575 us — it can compile before representative traces are learned, already documented in the threshold-zero note. Only adaptive `default` benefits.

## Notes

`docs/jit-internals.md` gains the committing-flush ownership contract.

items.title: Text-cleaning pipeline + context-aware per-cell field validation
items.body:
## Summary

Adds a production-grade **text data cleaning** layer and **context-aware per-cell field validation**, plus a root-cause fix in the core engine that stops a contaminated numeric column from passing through silently.

The driving scenario: a scraped feed inserts `"apple"` into different columns of a financial pipeline. The verdict must depend on the field —

| field | value | verdict |
|---|---|---|
| `transaction_amount` | `"apple"` | `semantic_mismatch` → quarantine (never coerced) |
| `company_name` | `"Apple"` / `"apple"` | valid — real-word names are never rejected for being words |
| `stock_ticker` | `"AAPL"` | valid; optional injected reference universe |
| `stock_ticker` | `"apple"` | `domain_mismatch`; suggests `AAPL` **only** from a caller-supplied trusted mapping |
| `transaction_description` | `"Payment to Apple"` | valid free text; spacing normalized, entity text preserved |
| numeric column + one `"apple"` | — | flagged with exact row/column even **without a schema** (column consensus) |

## What's in here (4 commits)

1. **`fix_dtypes` silence fix** (`steps/dtypes.py`): a column that is ≥60% numeric but blocked from conversion by a few unparseable cells (≤ max(3, 10%)) now emits a report warning naming the values and rows. Mixed alphanumeric ID columns (e.g. titanic `ticket`) stay silent. Nothing is coerced.
2. **`fd.clean_text` / `fd.clean_text_value` / `TextCleanConfig`** (`textclean.py`): deterministic ordered pipeline — Unicode NFC, control/zero-width/bidi stripping, punctuation normalization, optional HTML/URL removal, casing, repeat capping, truncation, custom ops. Input never mutated; every changed cell logged with original + cleaned + ordered transforms. **Field-aware**: lossy ops are automatically withheld from structural types (amounts, identifiers, emails, URLs, dates, tickers) and entity names. Stdlib + pandas only.
3. **`fd.validate_fields` / `FieldSpec` / `RemediationPolicy` / `fd.apply_field_policy`** (`fieldcheck.py`): per-cell validation combining declared specs (semantic type, range, vocabulary, pattern, per-field null markers, injected `reference`/`suggest`) with value shape and column consensus. Seven distinct failure classes (no generic "outlier" bucket); rare/extreme values are warned, never auto-rejected; configurable non-destructive actions (`accept` … `manual_review`); `apply_field_policy` splits accepted/quarantined/rejected/needs-review copies with a full audit trail. Vectorized per-column pre-screen keeps clean feeds at bulk speed; the per-cell explanation path runs only on suspects. Issues export as `QualityFinding` (step `fieldcheck`) into the existing quality-ops exporters.
4. **Docs + benchmark**: `docs/field-validation.md` (examples executed and verified against the API) and `benchmarks/bench_fieldcheck.py`, a seeded labeled-corruption benchmark.

## Benchmark (seeded, reproducible: `python benchmarks/bench_fieldcheck.py 100000`)

| validator | precision | recall | F1 | rows/s (100k) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| regex per column | 1.00 | 0.74 | 0.85 | ~499k |
| pandas coercion | 1.00 | 0.55 | 0.71 | ~1.3M |
| `fd.validate_fields` | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | ~118k |

Baselines miss out-of-range rates, unknown currencies and impossible-but-well-shaped dates; `validate_fields` catches all labeled corruptions at ~4× the cost of bare regex (after the vectorized pre-screen; it was ~130× before). Peak extra RSS at 100k rows: ~20 MB on a ~33 MB frame.

items.title: fix(setup): stop .env.example from hijacking the engine state dir
items.body:
## What changed?

- Removed the personal benchmark block (and a stray UTF-8 BOM) from the repo-root `.env.example`. Benchmark vars are already documented in `scripts/bench-js/.env.example`; a shared committed example must never pin the engine state directory.
- Hardened `ensureBootstrapEnv` in both `packages/tandem-control-panel/lib/setup/env.js` and the `packages/create-tandem-panel/template` copy so the `.env.example` merge can never contribute `TANDEM_STATE_DIR` / `TANDEM_CONTROL_PANEL_STATE_DIR` (or empty values). Real overrides still come from the user's own `.env` (`cwdEnv`) or the already-generated env file (`existing`), which both outrank the example.
- Added a regression test reproducing the poisoned-`.env.example` case.

## Why?

The repo-root `.env.example` (added in #1682) carried a developer's personal benchmark config, including:

```
TANDEM_STATE_DIR=%HOME%\work\tandem-engine\tandem\scripts\bench-js\.bench-state
```

`ensureBootstrapEnv` merges **every** key from a cwd `.env.example` into the generated env. Because that value is a truthy string it defeated the `|| paths.engineStateDir` default fallback. On Linux `%HOME%`/backslashes are not expanded, so the engine created a literal `<cwd>/%HOME%\work\...\.bench-state` directory and read/wrote **all** state there — making history, automations, and connections look wiped on every restart, with the correct data still sitting untouched at the default `~/.local/share/tandem`.

The state directories are computed per-platform and must be authoritative over any example value; `.env.example` is documentation, not a source of machine-specific values.

## How to test

- [x] `node --test packages/tandem-control-panel/tests/setup-init.test.mjs` — 5/5 passing, including the new `ignores a poisoned TANDEM_STATE_DIR in .env.example` case (verified it fails without the fix, passes with it)
- [x] `node --check` on both modified `env.js` files
- [x] Root `.env.example` no longer contains `bench-state` / `%HOME%` / `%USERPROFILE%` / `BENCH_*` / a BOM

## UX / Screenshots (if UI)

- N/A (setup/config only).

## Security considerations

- [x] No secrets added (removed a placeholder `BENCH_API_KEY` line from the shared example)
- [x] Permissions / filesystem rules unchanged or reviewed — this makes the engine's state directory resolution more predictable, not less

items.title: ci: A/B/C benchmark vs the C engine — PR impact comment + gh-pages dashboards
items.body:
## What

An opt-in benchmark pipeline that measures this repo's Rust port against the production **C engine** and publishes the gap — as GitHub Pages dashboards and an auto-updating PR comment.

On a PR it runs a three-way **A/B/C** comparison across **all dataset sizes**:

| | image | role |
|---|---|---|
| **A** | `docker.io/falkordb/falkordb-server:edge` | C engine — baseline |
| **B** | `ghcr.io/falkordb/falkordb-server:edge-rs` | published Rust (main, *without* this PR) |
| **C** | `ghcr.io/falkordb/falkordb-server:rc-pr-<N>` | this PR |

Because B is Rust *without* the PR and C is Rust *with* it, **B→C is exactly this PR's performance impact**, and **A/C** compares the branch to the C engine. It reuses [`FalkorDB/benchmark`](https://github.com/FalkorDB/benchmark) (pinned to `0cc0e9e`); each variant runs sequentially in a resource-capped container so numbers aren't skewed by neighbours.

## Entry points

- **PR** — add the `benchmark` label or comment `/benchmark` (OWNER/MEMBER/COLLABORATOR; same-repo branches only — a fork's read-only token can't publish). Posts/upserts one all-sizes impact comment and publishes to `/benchmark/branch/<slug>/`; the view is removed when the PR closes.
- **Manual** — the *A/B/C benchmark* workflow, arbitrary A/B image tags, single size.
- **Automatic** — on merge to `main`, the canonical `edge` vs `edge-rs` trend at `/benchmark/` (unbounded history; `small`, A/B).

## Architecture

```
_benchmark.yml   reusable engine
  ├─ benchmark   matrix over `sizes` — large → ubuntu-latest-16-cores, else 8-cores;
  │              each leg runs A/B/C and uploads a per-size summary
  └─ merge       publishes the dashboard once + upserts one all-sizes comment
benchmark.yml    front doors: label / /benchmark / dispatch (+ closed-PR cleanup)
rust-push.yml    canonical trend on merge (needs: promote-edge)
scripts/benchmark/
  run-ab.sh          docker + benchmark-CLI orchestration (N variants)
  publish.sh         Next.js static export → gh-pages layout
  patch-ui.sh        make the vendored ui/ relocatable under a sub-path
  gh-pages-push.sh   shared identity + token-remote + rebase-retry push
  update-manifest.py run-history index + retention pruning
  format-summary.py  A/B/C multi-size impact comment
  view-slug.sh       shared branch → view-slug (single source of truth)
```

The size legs run in parallel, so wall-clock ≈ the slowest leg, not the sum; the single merge job means no concurrent gh-pages writers and no comment pile-ups.

## Design decisions (settled)

- Comment leads with **B→C** (the PR's delta), **A/C** as context.
- **All ~35–39 read shapes**, **all three sizes** on size-appropriate runners.
- `cancel-in-progress: false` — the workflow listens to `issue_comment`, so `true` would let *any* PR comment cancel a ~90-min run (concurrency is evaluated before job-level `if`s).
- Waits on the **PR image (C)** landing in the registry — built early by `rust-pr.yml`, before its slower/flaky test jobs — not on the whole Rust PR run.

## Not in this PR (Phase 2)

Per-query "top movers" in the comment, and the **main-branch per-query trend** view (small-multiples + drill-down) — that one modifies the vendored Next.js UI and needs a separate design pass. Design mockup for both views was reviewed and signed off.

## Notes for review

- The big correctness point: **B is now `edge-rs`, C is the PR image** (previously B was the PR image).
- All external contracts (benchmark CLI subcommands/flags, the `ui/` source lines `patch-ui.sh` rewrites, the summary-JSON schema) are pinned and verified against `FalkorDB/benchmark@0cc0e9e`.
- Prerequisite: `ubuntu-latest-8-cores` **and** `ubuntu-latest-16-cores` Larger Runners provisioned for the org.
- Assumes `rc-pr`/`edge-rs` GHCR images are publicly pullable (no `docker login`) — same assumption throughout; confirm on the first labelled PR.

## Validation

actionlint clean on the restructured workflows · shellcheck clean on all `.github/scripts/benchmark/*.sh` (new `shellcheck.yml` gate) · `format-summary.py` and `run-ab.sh` exercised locally.

## Test plan

- [ ] Label a PR `benchmark` → three sizes run, dashboard published, one comment shows the A/B/C table with B→C per size.
- [ ] `/benchmark` comment adds the label and triggers the same path.
- [ ] Manual dispatch against two published tags.
- [ ] Merge to main updates the canonical `/benchmark/` trend.
- [ ] Close a labelled PR → its `/benchmark/branch/<slug>/` view is removed.

items.title: fix(memory): align fallback tokenizer minimum with FTS5 sanitizer
items.body:
## Summary
- `find_relevant()`'s token scan fallback in `persistent.py` required tokens of 3 characters or more, while the FTS5 query sanitizer in `search_index.py` accepted tokens of 2 characters or more, so short but meaningful queries (ticker symbols, country codes) silently returned nothing whenever `VT_MEMORY_FTS_INDEX` was disabled, even when the stored entry plainly contained the term.
- Widen the fallback tokenizer's minimum to 2 characters to match the FTS5 sanitizer, so retrieval no longer depends on which search path is active.

## Why
I audited every tokenizer used across the Tier 2 memory modules: `compression.py`, `semantic_links.py`, `persistent.py`, `search_index.py`, and the benchmark runner's own tokenizer. Only the `persistent.py` fallback creates a silent retrieval failure, since it is the only tokenizer whose minimum length diverges from the FTS5 path it stands in for. `compression.py`'s tokenizer only affects which sentences get kept during summarisation, not whether an entry can be found later. `semantic_links.py`'s tokenizer only affects BM25 linking between entries, a separate feature.

I reproduced this directly against real code checked out from upstream main before writing any fix. With an entry containing "GE reported strong earnings...", the fallback path returned zero results for the query "GE" while the FTS5 path found it correctly. Identical content, identical query, different result, based solely on the `VT_MEMORY_FTS_INDEX` flag.

## Changes
- `agent/src/memory/persistent.py`: widen the fallback tokenizer's minimum to 2 ASCII characters, matching the FTS5 sanitizer in `search_index.py`, with a comment explaining why the two need to stay in sync.
- `agent/src/memory/compression.py`: fix a docstring that claimed to use "the same regex pattern as persistent.py," which became inaccurate once `persistent.py`'s minimum changed. Comment only, no behaviour change.
- `agent/tests/memory/test_tier2_integration.py`: two new tests. One confirms the fallback path finds a short token entry on its own. The other confirms the fallback and FTS5 paths agree on the same short token query.
- `agent/tests/test_persistent_memory.py`: split the old `test_short_words_excluded` test, which pinned the previous 3 char minimum as correct behaviour, into a 1 char exclusion test (still correct) and a new 2 char inclusion test (the fixed behaviour).

## Test Plan
- [x] Reproduced the bug against real upstream code before writing any fix, confirming it was a genuine failure and not hypothetical
- [x] New regression tests fail on the pre-fix code with a concrete assertion failure (fallback returned 0 results instead of 1 for a "GE" query against an entry containing "GE"), and pass after the fix
- [x] `pytest agent/tests/memory/ agent/tests/test_persistent_memory.py -q` (150 passed, 1 skipped, no regressions)
- [x] Attempted the broader memory test selection, but collection was blocked by unrelated optional dependencies absent from the minimal environment. Ran the focused suites covering the changed memory paths instead: 150 passed, 1 skipped.
- [x] `black --check` on all four changed files: pre-existing, unrelated formatting issues confirmed via diff-isolation against the unpatched files; no full-file reformat applied, to avoid unrelated diff noise
- [x] `ruff check` on all four changed files: 3 pre-existing issues, all in `test_tier2_integration.py` (two unused imports, one unused variable), none introduced by this change, none in the other three files

## Checklist
- [x] No changes to protected areas (`src/agent/`, `src/session/`, `src/providers/`): this only touches `agent/src/memory/` and `agent/tests/`
- [x] No hardcoded values
- [x] Code follows CONTRIBUTING.md guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated: corrected the `compression.py` docstring that inaccurately claimed to match `persistent.py`'s tokenizer regex
- [x] DCO signed-off

items.body:
## What / Why

Issue #5935 (parent #5593, related closed #5602), discovered while gating PR #5931.

The canonical trace-predicate export lane (`robot_sf/benchmark/trace_predicate_export.py`) already accepts **both** `safety_predicate.late_evasive.v1` and `.v2` (it explicitly retains legacy provenance: `_SUPPORTED_PREDICATE_SCHEMAS["late_evasive"] = (v1, v2)`). But the scenario-evidence crosswalk (`robot_sf/benchmark/scenario_evidence_crosswalk.py`) registry recognized **only `.v2`**, so feeding a real legacy export through `build_scenario_evidence_crosswalk` failed closed with:

```
unknown predicate schema version 'safety_predicate.late_evasive.v1' for predicate 'late_evasive'
```

This blocked the documented downstream consumer (the crosswalk) from reading real, versioned, durable campaign artifacts.

### The decision (recorded, per DoD item 1)

**`safety_predicate.late_evasive.v1` is a supported crosswalk schema, retained as v1 (exact source provenance preserved, not normalized to v2).**

Evidence grounding the decision:
- The v1→v2 bump (PR #5063) is documented as an **additive** telemetry-instrumentation change — it adds `latency_unavailable_reason` and a seconds-valued latency — with explicit **"no benchmark metric semantics change"** and **"Existing consumers read `fields` via `.get(...)` and are unaffected."**
- The crosswalk's public contract records only **predicate identity + schema provenance + status**. It does **not** interpret `latency_unavailable_reason` or any field-level difference; the `late_evasive` boolean and predicate identity are identical between v1 and v2.
- The real durable issue4206 trace-capable bundle is **v1-only**: **6291 v1 records, 0 v2 records** across all 11 planner runs. The v2 schema currently exists only in code; no durable artifact uses it.
- This mirrors the producer's own philosophy ("retain its provenance") and the issue's expected behavior / risk mitigation, both of which say **"preserve exact source schema provenance."**

## Implementation

items.title: Guard-owner cache: make it opt-in, add multi-writer support
items.body:
## Summary

The guard-owner cache (which skips NIP-09/NIP-62 admission probes for owners with no stored tombstone/vanish) was load-once and invisible to writes from other processes. This made it unsafe for multi-writer deployments (e.g., a serving relay + sync router both feeding the same Vespa), where a second writer's tombstone would never be honoured. The fix makes the cache opt-in by default and adds refresh support for multi-writer topologies.

## Key Changes

- **New `WriterTopology` enum** (`WriterTopology.kt`): declares the deployment's write pattern to the store, since no store can detect a sibling feeder:
  - `SHARED_STRICT` (default): no cache; every insert probes NIP-09/NIP-62. Safe under any topology, trades read capacity for correctness.
  - `SINGLE_WRITER`: load-once cache, no refresh. Fast path with no staleness window, but asserts this process is the only writer for its owners.
  - `SHARED`: cache rebuilt on an interval, so foreign tombstones are honoured within one refresh. Bounded window acceptable for multi-writer deployments.

- **`GuardOwners` refactored** to support all three modes:
  - Added `refresh()` method: rebuilds both guard sets from the corpus (union-only, never unflagging an owner).
  - Added background refresher under `SHARED` mode, started with the first load.
  - Buffering of guards noted during a rebuild (`Noted` class): a guard stored while the scan is in flight is folded into the replacement before it is published, preventing false negatives introduced by the fix itself.
  - Environment override `GUARD_OWNERS_DISABLE` now forces `SHARED_STRICT` and validates its documented values (`1`, `true`, `yes`, `on`) — unparseable values fail loudly instead of silently ignoring them.

- **`NostrSemanticsStore` updated**:
  - Added `writers` parameter (defaults to `WriterTopology.SHARED_STRICT`).
  - Added `guardRefreshMillis` parameter for `SHARED` mode cadence.
  - Added `refreshGuardOwners()` public method: on-demand barrier for deployments that know when a foreign write occurred (e.g., after a sync round).
  - Passes topology and refresh interval to `GuardOwners`.

- **`VespaEventStore.open()` updated**:
  - Added `writers` parameter (defaults to `WriterTopology.SHARED_STRICT`).
  - Added `guardRefreshSeconds` parameter.
  - Exposed `refreshGuardOwners()` as a public method.

- **Comprehensive test suite** (`GuardOwnersMultiWriterTest.kt`):
  - Tests the acceptance case: a second writer's tombstone blocks after a refresh.
  - Tests background refresher: staleness is bounded by the interval, not process lifetime.
  - Tests the default topology blocks immediately (no cache).
  - Tests `SINGLE_WRITER` mode: loaded sets stand for process lifetime (and documents the consequence of violating the assertion).
  - Tests union-only rebuild: a guard noted during a rebuild survives the swap.
  - Tests environment override parsing: documented values are accepted, unparseable values fail.

- **Documentation updates** (`docs/multi-node-consistency.md`, `docs/server-side-constraints.md`, `README.md`, `benchmark/README.md`):
  - Explains the guard-owner cache failure mode and the three topologies.
  - Clarifies that the cache is a pure performance device whose only failure is serving a deleted event.
  - Documents the rebuild cost (distinct-author scan per guard kind, scales with corpus size, not guard count).
  - Notes that `SHARED` rebuild duration on a large corpus is the binding term of the staleness window, not the configured interval.

## Notable Implementation Details

- **Union-only rebuild**: the swap is protected by `swapLock`, and guards noted during the scan are buffered in `Noted` and folded in before the replacement is published. This prevents a false negative that would be introduced by the fix itself.

items.title: perf(codegen): prove array-index ranges for strided counters and constant-argument parameters (#7286)
items.body:
Closes #7286 (levers **a** and **c**; lever **b** was already present and is now reachable).

`crates/perry-codegen/src/expr/index_get.rs`'s `numeric_index_needs_runtime_key` demotes an
array access to the fully opaque `js_array_get_index_or_string` /
`js_typed_feedback_array_set_index_or_string` helpers unless the index carries a
`[0, i32::MAX]` range proof. Two extremely common shapes had no way to produce one:

* a **strided induction counter** — `for (let j = i * i; j < LIMIT; j = j + i)` — only
  `i++` with an integer-literal start was classified;
* a **numeric parameter** — `matmul(a, b, c, size: number)` arrives as a bare NaN-boxed
  `double` with no fact, and ranges compose through `+`/`*`, so one unbounded leaf
  poisons `i * size + k` and demotes *every* array access in the function.

## What changed

**Lever (a) — monotone-induction range** (`crates/perry-codegen/src/stmt/counter_range.rs`, new).
`classify_for_counter_range` moved out of the 7k-line `loops.rs` and gained the
`j = j + <stride>` step shape. A counter whose only writer is the loop's update slot and
whose step never decreases it is bounded above by the (re-evaluated) loop guard and below
by its initial value. Admission requires: a non-negative *integral* start, a non-negative
*integral* stride, and the stride's operands loop-invariant and not closure-captured. The
classifier now also refuses a fact when the **body** writes the counter — a hole the old
`i++` path had (`for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) { a[i]; i = -5; }` re-enters the body with
`i === -4`).

**Lever (c) — interprocedural parameter ranges** (`crates/perry-codegen/src/collectors/param_ranges.rs`, new).
A whole-module pre-pass meets the argument constants over *all* call sites of a function
whose entire call graph is visible. Any unresolved reference poisons it: exported,
reflected onto `globalThis`, `FuncRef` used as a value, `Expr::Closure` with the same id,
arity mismatch, rest/default/`arguments` parameters, a parameter that is written or
rebound anywhere, a duplicated `FuncId`, or a single non-constant argument. The summary
feeds `int_range_for_local` as a last resort.

**Lever (b)** — `int_range_expr` already composes `a * b + c`; it simply never had ranges
for the leaves. With (c) supplying `size`, `i * size + k` proves `[0, 65535]` on its own.

## Measured (Apple M1 Max, **release** build both arms, identical runtime archives, `PERRY_NO_AUTO_OPTIMIZE=1`)

Host was **not idle** (1-min load average 5.8 on 10 cores — other agents building), so absolute
numbers carry some noise; the five-run spreads below are tight and the effect is an order of
magnitude, well outside it. Node reference is v22.23.1 from `~/.cache/perry-bench-tools`
(benchmark-only pin), as in #7286.

| benchmark | before (5 runs) | after (5 runs) | | node |
|---|---:|---:|---|---:|
| `16_matrix_multiply` | 708 693 689 692 696 | **70 70 69 70 70** | **9.9x** | 40 |
| `11_prime_sieve` | 119 118 117 135 118 | **29 31 32 33 31** | **3.8x** | 6 |
| `15_mandelbrot` | 23 23 23 22 22 | 23 23 22 23 22 | unchanged | |
| `05_fibonacci` | 408 408 408 415 407 | 407 408 408 405 411 | unchanged | |

`16_matrix_multiply` goes from 17.3x behind node to **1.8x**; `11_prime_sieve` from 19.7x to 5.2x.
Checksums byte-identical (`41079519680`, `primes:78498`), and all 30 benchmarks in
`benchmarks/suite/` produce identical output.

The two compiler binaries hash differently
(`948fb4ed…` vs `173b781c…`) and both arms link the **same** `libperry_runtime.a` /
`libperry_stdlib.a`, so the delta is codegen and nothing else.

## IR evidence

`matmul`'s innermost block `for.body.23`, before:

```llvm
%r103 = call double @js_array_get_index_or_string(i64 %r102, double %r100)
%r104 = call double @js_number_coerce(double %r103)
%r115 = call double @js_array_get_index_or_string(i64 %r114, double %r112)
%r116 = call double @js_number_coerce(double %r115)
```

After: **zero `js_*` calls** in the block — `fptosi` + a header tag test, then a branch into
the inline guarded deref. Every remaining `js_*` in the function sits on an
`arr.guard.cold.*` / `arr.fallback.*` / `idxset.*` edge. That is 4 opaque calls × 256³ =
**67.1M calls removed**.

`prime_sieve`'s `sieve[j] = false` (`for.body.44`) loses
`js_typed_feedback_array_set_index_or_string` *and* the array-pointer re-anchoring
(`store double %r266, ptr %r8`) that followed it; the store is now an inline i32 bounds
check plus `store double`.

## Soundness

Every admission is a proof, not a heuristic; anything unproven keeps the runtime-key path.
Notably this is **not** about `i32`-ness — `(i * size + k) | 0` is a genuine `i32` and
buys nothing, because `ToInt32`'s `[-2^31, 2^31-1]` has `min < 0`. The `& 0x7fffffff` mask
used to *measure* the prize in #7286 is not shipped: it changes semantics for negative and
`>= 2^31` indices.

`test-files/test_gap_array_index_range_proof.ts` (16 cases) is byte-identical to Node
26.5.1 on: negative / fractional / `NaN` / `-0` indices, `2^32-2` vs `2^32-1` vs `2^32`,
indices above `i32::MAX`, an affine index that overflows `i32`, holey and sparse arrays,
a body write to the counter, a body write to the stride, a callee that reassigns its
parameter, a callee that escapes as a value, a non-integral stride, and an `+Infinity`
start. It passes on `main` too, so it is a genuine non-regression gate.

25 new `cargo-test`-visible `--lib` unit tests (11 for the counter classifier, 14 for the
parameter collector), all in `src/` so they run per-PR. `cargo test -p perry-codegen --lib`:
573 passed, 0 failed.

## Whole-corpus differential

Every one of the **474 `test-files/test_gap_*.ts`** programs was compiled with the baseline
compiler and with this branch — against the *same* runtime archives — run, and their
stdout+stderr+exit code compared. **474/474 identical.** 13 needed the normalisation the real
parity harness applies anyway (thread ids, raw backtrace addresses, sub-millisecond
`console.time` values); those 13 were re-checked serially and are byte-identical modulo those
fields. Since the baseline's node-parity is already pinned by `test-parity/gap_snapshot.json`,
"identical to baseline" is "identical to node" everywhere the snapshot says the baseline matches.

Local `lint`-job gates all green: `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `check_file_size.sh`,
`gc_store_site_inventory.py`, `addr_class_inventory.py`, `workspace_architecture.py`,
`test_public_baseline.py`, `ci_public_baseline_check.py`, `check_test_registration.py`,
`cargo clippy -p perry-codegen --lib`.

items.title: repsel: one safety gate and one write walker for both numeric proofs, plus the #7770 super-chain test and bench numbers
items.body:
Follow-up to #7774 (merged as 2e5bf4434). These two commits were pushed to the PR branch but were not in the rebase that got merged, so they are absent from `main`; the branch was deleted on merge, so this restores them. **No behavior change** — a consolidation, a coverage gap, and two efficiency items, all from the code review of #7774.

## 1. One safety gate, not two (the load-bearing one)

`prove_group_numeric_fields` had grown its own copy of the `'cand` loop's entire Pass-3 obligation set: `ThisFlowAnalysis` construction, `ctor_chain_safe`, `prototype_is_stable`, field/method name-ambiguity, per-method `method_safe`. That verdict is what licenses a **bare unchecked `load double`**, so the two copies silently drifting is a miscompile, not a missed optimization — and nothing diffed them against each other.

Extracted as `chain_this_flow_verdict`, now the single implementation both callers use. Tightening an obligation is a one-place change again.

## 2. The super-chain resolution path had no test at group scope

`prove_numeric_fields` resolves a parent constructor's parameters through `super(...)` argument lists under the **caller's** already-resolved environment. #7774 made that path reachable through the group MEET (multiple provenance `new`s) for the first time, and every fixture in the new test file had `extends: None` — so a wrong index or an unresolved caller env there would have granted an unsound claim with zero red tests.

`super_chain_params_resolve_under_the_group_meet` covers both directions: all-numeric push sites prove the derived *and* the inherited field; one string at the super-feeding position drops exactly `z` group-wide while `x` survives.

## 3. One write walker, not three

`collect_numeric_by_construction_locals` had a hand-rolled full `Stmt`-tree write collector nearly identical to `not_bigint_locals::collect_writes` — the "two traversals that must agree, drifting by one `Stmt` variant" bug class that `ptr_shape_elements.rs`'s own doc warns this file cannot afford. Generalized `collect_writes` to record a no-init `Let` as `None` (fine for the non-BigInt fixpoint, fatal for the numeric one) and deleted the duplicate.

- The group proof ran its full this-flow walk before discovering the class has no raw-f64-declared field anywhere on the chain (proven arrays of string/object-only records paid for a moot proof). Now bails first.
- `group_members()` rebuilt its map twice per collector run — once for the numeric proof, once for the pre-existing group-integrity pass. Computed once, passed to both.

## 5. The perf numbers for #7770

The merged fragment stops before the bench results. Restores them: on the pinned quiet mini (interleaved arms, best-of-15, two independent runs, outputs byte-verified against Node before timing) the issue's read loop goes **101/102 ms → 91/90 ms**, while `batch.ts`, `suite/04_array_read` and `suite/09_method_calls` are unchanged.
